utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning to those here and good morning to those waiting in Pristina.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Via videolink] Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Popaj is there, I see.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Via videolink] Yes, Your Honour, he is. We can hear you loud and clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Splendid.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Via videolink] However, I can only hear the Albanian channel. If one of our technicians would be able to call on the office channel here, I would be able to get the English channel as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. We hope that will be corrected, but in the meantime would you show the witness the affirmation card if you have it. I would say to the witness, do you affirm that the evidence you will give will be the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The witness appears to be speaking to us, but we hear no sound.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I declare to speak the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Please sit down. I see that our telephone call has now reached the Court Officer. He may be able to hear me in an English translation from now on. Now, we have some questions for you this morning, and I will start by asking Mr. Behar to continue with some questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Good morning, sir. Thank you very much for joining us this morning. I know it wasn't easy for you to be here today. Sir, can we begin by having you state your full name and date of birth for the record.

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: I am Sabri Popaj. I was born on the 5th of August, 1959.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: I understand, sir, that you were born and you grew up in Bela Crkva, in the Rahovec municipality; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Sir, I understand that on the 12th, 13th, and 14th of June of 1999 you gave a statement to the Office of the Prosecutor about the events that you experienced in Kosovo; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And I understand that you also made certain corrections or clarifications to that statement on the 5th of June, 2002; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Have you had the opportunity to read those statements before coming to court today?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And other than the changes that you made previously when you testified in the Milutinovic case, are you satisfied that the information that's contained in those statements is true and accurate to the best of your knowledge and belief?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: Yes, it is true and accurate.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would seek to tender that statement and the addendum as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: They will be received.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Yes, the 65 ter number they're both under 02445 [sic].

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be P01082.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Sir, do you recall testifying at the trial of Milan Milutinovic on the 1st and 2nd of November of 2006?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And did you have a chance to review the transcript of your testimony in that trial?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: I understand there are a couple of things that you'd like to clarify that are presently recorded in the transcript. I'll take you to those sections and I'll just ask for your comments. I'm going to be referring to the transcript which is at 65 ter 5338, but I'll just read them aloud to you, sir, so we can have the translation. My first reference is at page 5667 and lines 7 and 8 read: "Later on we took the body of Feim Popaj, Alban Popaj, Hysni Popaj, and Qamil Zhuniqi and took their bodies to Xerxe ..." I understand there was a clarification or a correction you would like to make to that, sir?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Just before you do. Mr. Popovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. In principle, we object to this kind of introducing corrections to the transcript, as testified in the Milutinovic case. We believe the Prosecutor could have done this differently by putting questions that were put in the original transcript and the witness could have corrected the things he thought necessary, but correcting in this way with the other possibility existing we believe is not in the interests of justice. That was the gist of my objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. I think something similar has been objected several times in the past. As a matter of principle, we do not agree. We would agree if the correction was being suggested by counsel. All he is doing is saying there is a passage we understand you wish to correct and leaving it to the witness to indicate what change the witness proposes. And on that basis, we think it a convenient and practical method to proceed. Yes, Mr. Behar, please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Mr. Popaj, do you want me to read to you that passage again or are you able to answer?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: I can make the correction now. These people were not bodies, dead bodies, but they were survivors. Hysni Popaj and Alban Popaj died later. The other people are still living.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And just to focus you again on that, sir. When you -- those names there, and I'll read them to you Feim Popaj, Alban Popaj, Hysni Popaj and Qamil Zhuniqi -- maybe I should read you the section just to give you the context.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: If I could just have a moment's indulgence.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: So your answer was: "My wife went to the spot and saw that they were all executed, then she returned. She came to me and she told me that everybody was executed. Later on we took the body of Feim Popaj, Alban Popaj, Hysni Popaj, and Qamil Zhuniqi and took their bodies to Xerxe." Now, again, sir, can you comment on what if anything you wanted to change about that?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: Yes, the correction is this: Qamil Zhuniqi was dead there, and we did not take his body. Sezai Zhuniqi, we took him. Alban Popaj, Hysni Popaj, Shukri Gashi, he also was wounded --

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Right. So I think you've now made a couple of changes, sir. Just let me know if I have this correct. It says "body" there, but you are indicating that you were taking the bodies of survivors; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: Yes, they were alive. Eight people were alive when we took them. Two of them died. One of them died at 6.00 p.m., while the other one died on the 26th at 1.00 p.m. -- 1.00 a.m.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Thank you. And there was a second thing I think you changed was that the name Qamil Zhuniqi you've given us a new name you say that should be Sezai Zhuniqi; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: Sezai Zhuniqi, yes. And he died in 2006.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. My next reference is to page 5679 of the transcript. Just very briefly, lines 10 and 11 here, sir, they were part of a question that you went on to answer in your testimony and the question read: "And if you could explain, how could you see the explosion of all three churches, as you say in your correction today?" Is there something you wanted to clarify about that question and your subsequent answer?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: My answer was three mosques not three churches. There are no churches in Bellacerka, Rogove, or Celine, there have never been.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Next, my next reference is at page 5685. Line 25 on that page, sir, states: "In Celine it was either on the 12th or 13th of April when they brought the eight bodies ..." And then it says: "They brought Sefedin Sahani with his entire family ..." Is there something you want to say about that?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: Sefedin Hasani. Setadin Hasani with five members of his family: Muhamet Rexhepi, Hajdar Rexhepi, and Sakip Rexhepi. These were the eight people that were brought.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Thank you. And just for the transcript is it correct was it Setadin Hasani, S-e-t-a-d-i-n, that you said?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: Hasani, yes, yes, that's the name, Setadin Hasani.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. And the final comment I'll ask you for is at page 5708. At lines 16 and 17 you state: "That is true because until the 4th of May, I was in Xerxe. On the 4th of May, the inhabitants of Xerxe left in the direction of Potoqan ..." Is there something that you'd like to explain about that line, sir?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: On the 4th of May, the people of Xerxe were forced out of their village and they were sent in the direction of Prizren and then towards Albania.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And so, in your testimony, sir, where it refers to Potoqan there, are you able to say what you intended by that or why, to your knowledge, it may have said "Potoqan" at that point?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: I did not say that. They did not go towards Potoqan. They went towards Prizren and then Albania.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you, sir. Having made those comments for us, sir, does the transcript now accurately reflect your evidence and would you testify to those same facts again today?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: My testimony is correct and it reflects what I saw and experienced myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would seek to tender that transcript it's 65 ter 05338.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit P01083.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Thank you. And just a quick note, Your Honour, I think I misspoke earlier when I referenced the 65 ter number for the statements, I believe it was 02446, and I may have said 02445. Your Honours, I would also like to tender a number of exhibits that were tendered in association with Mr. Popaj's testimony in the Milutinovic case. I can go through them. There's about eight. And I can just provide the number and a brief description. The first four exhibits are aerial photographs that were marked by the witness in his prior testimony. The first is 05018.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Are you proposing these be dealt with separately?

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: I think that's easiest if it's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Very well, that will be received. Sorry, Mr. Popovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, Defence does have to object to this way of seeking to tender such documents. First of all, these are aerial images that the witness marked certain things on. The explanation as to what the marked locations are is in the transcript of the Milutinovic case; however, if we look at the transcript we can conclude that after that it was absolutely unclear what it was that was marked on the maps and photographs and what the reason for marking them was. I can agree with the fact that this can be further clarified by Defence, but I believe it would be more purposeful and simple if the witness ... First of all, we are talking about four aerial photographs of Bela Crkva, I don't mean the two photographs with the mosques in which he marked minarets; that is not something we object to. But the remaining four photographs with the numbers and marked roads and little squares, realistically speaking, do not tell us much. For the Chamber to have a full insight into what it was that the witness marked, we believe it would be advisable for the witness to repeat the exercise and mark those things on the photographs again. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Popovic. There are two things here. The first is for the Chamber to fully understand the evidence of the witness given at the previous trial, and these exhibits are ones which the witness refers to specifically in his evidence and marks and explains those markings in the transcript. Now, for us then to understand his evidence at the trial, these aerial photographs are relevant for that purpose. The second purpose is for us to understand fully for the purposes of our present trial what relevance those photographs may have. The two objectives will often be met by the one photograph and one marking, but if it is the view of counsel that there is something material to this trial which is unclear from the transcript and the markings, that is a matter which should be dealt with in this trial as a matter of clarification of the evidence. And that is in part what is being done at the moment by the Prosecution, and in due course you will have an opportunity in cross-examination to do the same if it is felt that there is something about the marking which is unclear or incomplete or wrong for the purposes of our present trial. So at least for the moment on the basis of understanding and receiving the evidence given at the previous trial, we will receive these exhibits.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 65 ter 05018 will be Exhibit P01084.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: The next aerial photograph is 05019.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 05019 will be Exhibit P01085, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And then 05020.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That too will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit P01086, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, it will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit P01087.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: The next exhibit 00094, those are photographs of victims of the Bela Crkva massacre as identified by the witness in Milutinovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Those photographs will be Exhibit P01088, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Two following exhibits are marked photographs of mosques 5022.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit P01089, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit P01090.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And then there are two final photographs, aerial photographs, that were marked by the witness. The first is 05024.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit P01091, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And the final exhibit is 05025.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit P01092, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I can just note briefly for the record there are two exhibits that were reference that we're not seeking to tender because they're already in evidence. 65 ter 01800 is currently in evidence as P00638. And 65 ter number 02445 is already in evidence as P00634.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Thank you. I can now provide a summary of Mr. Popaj's evidence. Mr. Popaj is a Kosovar Albanian Muslim from the village of Bela Crkva in the municipality of Rahovec. He describes the presence of Serb police and military in the week prior to the 24th of March, 1999, and he describes that on the 25th of March, 1999, tanks set up positions overlooking the village and automatic weapons were fired towards the village. He describes helping 14 civilians to cross Belles stream that day. After leaving the group, he saw Serb policemen approaching the steam, shooting, and shouting obscenities. He observed these police open fire on the civilians with their automatic rifles. He watched as police later killed an old man who they found hiding. After they had left, he went to the stream and observed the bodies of the people who had been killed. Mr. Popaj then watched as the police searched and took identification and valuables from 45 to 50 civilian men near the railway bridge by the stream. His brother and his sons were among those men. He watched as the police then opened fire on those men. Mr. Popaj later returned with civilians from Xerxe and helped to bring several people who had managed to survive the massacre into the town. He returned to the stream again the next day and helped to bury the bodies and record the names of those who had died. In the days that followed, Mr. Popaj observed the aftermath of a number of further massacres. He observed a number of scenes where villagers had been shot and burned in the town of Celina and assisted in burying a large number of bodies. He describes the work done by Agim Jemini and others. Mr. Popaj also made observations of destruction in Nagavc and subsequently described police involved in burying bodies near Celina. He described the destruction of mosques. And he also describes how he left Kosovo on the 13th of May, 1999, and how at the border he observed police demand identification and then burn it. That is the end of the summary.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Sir, I do have some brief questions for you in the time that we have remaining. First, I know that you've described in detail how you observed these massacres that took place at the Belles stream. I'd like to ask you some questions about the timing of what happened after that, and if possible I'd like to be clear about the order that the things happened in. Now, first you described that after seeing the massacre you saw your mother, father, and your wife on the railway tracks and that you went and joined them. And you described that your wife went back to the stream and told you that nine people had survived the shooting. Am I correct so far?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: Yes, you are.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Okay. Now, you describe as well that you, your mother, your father, and your wife walked to Zrze. My question for you, sir, is: Did all of you go all the way to Zrze at that time?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: No. After we took the wounded, I stayed at the railway track. My wife and my father and mother went to take the tractor together with Shemsedin Kelmendi. They came back. We took the survivors, put them on the tractor, and then took them to Abaz Kryeziu's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Okay. So let me make sure that I'm understanding that correct. So you described, you stayed at the railway track; your wife, your father, and your mother went to take a tractor with Shemsedin Kelmendi and came back. Just so we're clear, sir, then, before you went -- well, did you yourself go all the way to Zrze?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: No, we didn't go together in -- to Xerxe. I stayed there.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: I see. And so then when you described these people returning, am I understanding right then that those people -- so your mother, your father, and your wife went to Zrze. Can you tell us then who came back from Zrze and how?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: Yes, my wife returned and my father, but not my mother. My aunt did, the -- Abaz Kryeziu and the driver Shemsedin Kelmendi.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And you mentioned a tractor as well. Did they come back with the tractor at this point?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: They returned to pick up the wounded with tractor. When we went to Xerxe, we all walked. Only the driver was driving the tractor.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Right. And again, just so we're clear, we just received translation that said "when we went to Xerxe we all walked ..." But you just described you yourself didn't go all the way to Zrze; am I understanding that right?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: I waited for my wife to return with my father and with the tractor and with my aunt, to pick up the wounded at the site of the event. Then we went to pick up the wounded and went to Xerxe to take them to Xerxe.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Thank you very much. I think that's quite clear now. So when you met up then with the people that you just described and with the tractor, and I know that in your statement you describe returning to the scene and you describe them returning to the scene to bring back the survivors. Just so we're clear, were you at the scene with them and did you insist in bringing back the survivors at that time?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: Yes, I returned with them along with a tractor. In Xerxe I helped the wounded, but unfortunately one died and Alban, my nephew, died later in the morning of the next day. And we buried them in the yard of Abaz Kryeziu's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Sir, you also mentioned the Zhuniqi family in your statement and you referred to Isuf Zhuniqi in your prior testimony. Can you tell us, did you know the Zhuniqi family and did you know Isuf Zhuniqi in particular?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: Yes, I knew Isuf Zhuniqi because we were classmates from the first grade to the eighth grade.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And did you also know the Zhuniqi family?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: Yes, I have, because the Zhuniqi family -- my nephew was married to a girl from that family. So I knew them from a long time ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: After the massacre, sir, when was it that you saw or that you heard Isuf Zhuniqi? Can you explain that?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: After the massacre, the day, I was talking with my wife, my mother, and my father, and Isuf Zhuniqi was on the other side of the railway and I heard him shouting. And I said, What happened? And he simply moved his hands and didn't say anything and he left. He meant by that that they have executed everyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: That's what you understood that gesture to mean?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: Yes. He made with his hands like this.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And you described --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: For the record, I would intervene, Mr. Behar --

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: -- the witness placed both hands in front of him at the level of his chest with the palms down and moved them horizontally, one across the other and back. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Sir, you had referred in your prior answer to the fact that after the massacre that day you were talking with your wife, your mother, and your father. Am I correct then that you're referring to the time that -- in your statement where after seeing what you'd first seen, you then joined your mother, your father, and your wife, as you described in your statement?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. At that moment Isuf passed by on the other side of the railway shouting.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And can you explain to us where Isuf Zhuniqi had come from when you saw him?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: When you go to the place of the event, I was on the left-hand, he was on the right-hand-side and he passed by the railway in the direction of Xerxe.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And just let me know what -- only referring to what you actually saw, but was he coming from the place where you saw the massacre, was he coming from nearby, or from somewhere else? Are you able to say where you saw him coming from in that particular level of detail?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: He was coming from the place where the massacre happened, from where he had survived.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. I notice from your statement that there was a list of survivors in your statement at page 5, and I notice that Isuf Zhuniqi isn't listed with those other survivors on that page. Are you able to explain to us why that is?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: I don't know. Maybe he has given a statement himself. That's why he wasn't included in the list. I think. I don't know. Isuf -- we didn't pick up him with our tractor. I wrote down only the names of those that we pick up that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you, sir. And I think that's helpful. Sir, you're saying that those are the people that you picked up -- that's a list of the people you picked up with the tractor or the survivors you picked up with the tractor; am I understanding correctly?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: Isuf wasn't one of them that we took with us.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Right. And am I understanding correctly, sir, that you took the people listed back on your tractor, but Isuf Zhuniqi you did not? You described him passing away or running away. Am I understanding correctly that he left at that point, he left the scene?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. He went in the direction of Xerxe. When we went to Xerxe, I met him there but we didn't take him with us along with the tractor.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. I have a couple final questions about the manner in which you described crossing the border. When you left for Albania, you described in your statement the persons that you dealt with at the border as Serb border guards. I'm wondering if you can explain to us what type of forces those were that you dealt with at the border, if you know.

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: They were Serb police forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And are you able to tell us how you know that, how you could tell that they were police forces?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: From their uniforms we could tell that they were police forces, and it was written here "police."

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And finally --

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: There was a band written "police."

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Finally you describe your identification documents being thrown into a fire in your statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: The reference for my friend is in the B/C/S statement page 11, paragraph 9.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Can I ask you, sir, when you describe the identification documents being thrown into a fire, is that something you saw yourself?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I saw it with my own eyes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And are you able to explain to us where the fire was or how it was exactly that they did that so the Judges can understand?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: When we arrived at the border, they stopped us. The police came and asked us, Where are you from? And there were a lot of women from Peje. I said, I don't have documents, and asked those who were on the tractor if they had. And they showed me the documents and I gave them to this officer. He went, walked about 2 metres, and threw them on the fire. He said, We won't need these documents anymore from now on.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And again, just so we understand, when you say "threw them on the fire," was there a fire there that was already burning or can you describe where the fire was?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: There was a fire already when we arrived because there had been other people passing the border before us. There was a man. There was a glass jar there.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And just so I understand, you made reference to a glass jar. Are you able to explain to us what the significance of that was?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: It was not a glass jar, it was a metal kind of jar. We use them as a tanker in Kosova. It was used to light the fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: I see.

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: I apologise for saying glass.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: No, that's fine, sir, and we translate things into many languages here so sometimes that happens. That's fine. Thank you very much, sir, for your patience in answering my questions, and my learned friend from the Defence will have some questions for you now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Behar. Mr. Popovic, do you cross-examine?

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Popaj. My name is Aleksandar Popovic, one of the Defence counsel for Mr. Vlastimir Djordjevic. I'm going to ask you some questions. Mr. Popaj, please, before we start, I will try to make my questions as clear and as brief as possible, and if you have any suggestions concerning my questions you are free to express them. Mr. Popaj, if I'm not mistaken, you gave your statement on 12th, 13th, and 14th of June, 1999; am I right in saying so?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: This is a statement that you gave immediately after the event, some months after the event. Am I right in saying that your memory was the freshest then?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: My memory will always remain indelible, the memory of what I went through, until I die myself and join them.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: All right. So I will -- I will stick to that statement dated June 1999 and this will provide the basis for my questions today. But before I do so, please, could you confirm that you provided testimony in the Milosevic trial in 2002; is that right?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: When you provided that testimony, you had occasion to see once again the 1999 statement and to correct or introduce corrections if necessary; is that right?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Am I right in saying that in November 2006 in the Milutinovic trial you also testified, and to cut a long story short, on that occasion you also had an opportunity to see the 1999 statement and introduce some supplementary facts or corrections if there was a need to do so?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: That's correct too.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Please bear that in mind then and let us try to clarify some of the unclear matters there. First of all, I'm going to ask you how many inhabitants did your village -- was home to in 1999?

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Were there any members of Serb ethnicity in your village?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: All right. In your June 1999 statement, paragraph 5, page 2, it is stated that you understand that you are required to describe events that you witnessed yourself and to emphasise those parts of your statements that you heard from others. Did you bear that in mind when you were giving this statement?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: I gave statement only about what I witnessed myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In your June 1999 statement, page 1, paragraph 4, you discuss the KLA and your knowledge about them. I'm going to ask you some questions concerning that. In paragraph 4 you say: "There were three members of the KLA in our village whom everyone knew ..." Am I right that you stated so?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: They were not in the village. They were far away from the village. In 1998 from the 20th of May to the 20th of October I was staying in the mountains, but I heard in the village people saying that there were three KLA members.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Popaj, I'm going to read again what is stated in your statement, and I recently asked you whether you had opportunity on three occasions to review your statement and rectify it. So it is stated in your witness statement: "There were three members of the KLA in our village whom everyone knew ..." In none of your statements or testimonies have you said that somebody else told you about the presence of those three KLA members. Can you explain the reasons why is this -- this is so?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: I already stated that I personally didn't see these three people, but I heard that there were three members of the KLA but they were never actually in the village for me to see them. Even in the Milutinovic case when I testified, I already said that I didn't see these people myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: So this sentence "there were three members of the KLA in our village whom everyone knew ..." is not a true statement?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: It is not true that they were in the village. If they were in Drenica or somewhere else, this I don't know. I'm just saying that they were not present in the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Popaj, this was not my question. My question was: Did you give this statement and did you have occasion to rectify it on several occasions? I'm repeating my question. Am I right in saying that the sentence "there were three KLA members in our village whom everyone knew ..." is not true? Please answer my question.

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: It is not correct what you are putting to me. They were not in the village, but we knew that they were from our village. There were three members of the KLA. This is correct, but they were not in the village. And I said so even when I was here before. There were no KLA units in our village.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: I'm just confronting you with what is written in your statement, but let's not waste any more time on that. My next question is going to be the following: Did you know those three KLA members that you are discussing?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: I knew them but I didn't see them.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell us their names?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: At the time I didn't know the names. It was later on that I learned who they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: But in responding to the previous question you said: "I knew them but I did not see them." Now you say that at the time you did not know them. Which is the truth? Did you know them or did you not know them; and if you knew them, what were their names?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: I didn't know them personally. I learned their names after the war. At that time I didn't know that they were those -- the ones that were in the KLA. I know all the village inhabitants, but at that moment I didn't know that they were the three particular ones.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, but a minute ago you said: "I knew them but I didn't see them." When did you speak the truth, a minute ago or now? Now you're saying that you didn't know them.

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: I said it clearly, sir. I heard people say, and there is no one in the village that I don't know. But I didn't know who these three persons were. I learned that after the war, I learned their names. I simply knew that there were three members.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Did you ever see those three KLA members wearing uniforms?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: This is the right question you should have asked me. I never saw these three people in uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Then I would like us to take a look at the transcript in the Milutinovic case.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, we just received the number. P01082, if I'm not very much mistaken -- no, it's 083 the last three digits. Let's take a look at page 5697, line 23.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Popaj, in responding to questions put to you by Judge Bonomy in the Milutinovic case, trying to clarify the same matter that I'm trying to clarify now on whether there were three KLA members in your village whom everyone knew, you replied as follows: "Well, what I said is that three people from my village were in the KLA. They had uniforms ..." How did you learn that they had uniforms?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: After I returned from Albania I saw them. From 1998 to June 1999 I didn't know who they were. I never said that I knew them at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Popaj, you'll have to --

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: I can tell you the names because I learned that in 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: You will have to tell us not only the names but much more beyond that because what you are saying right now cannot be in any way compared to what you said before. Let's cut to the chase. What is true? What you've testified in the Milutinovic case where you said that there were three people from your village who were in the KLA and had uniforms, or what you're saying today when you said that you saw them only after returning from Albania and that from 1998 to 1999 you never knew who they were? Although you just a couple of minutes ago said that you knew them. This is complete confusion. Could you tell us, please, now, which of those statements are true?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: Sir, I am telling you that I knew every one of the inhabitants of the village, even today I do. And I told you that I didn't know who these three KLA members were in 1989 -- until 1989 I didn't know who they were when I returned home.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Correction 1998, 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: For the transcript do you mean 1998? Mr. Popaj, you said that they wore uniforms, and then in your response today you said you knew them. How do you have that knowledge? How come you said in the Milutinovic case three years ago that they had uniforms, and today in answering the questions you say that they -- that you don't know whether they had any uniforms? I didn't ask you about the period after 1998. You were quite precise when answering Judge Bonomy's question.

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: That I knew them from the day they were born, of course, and I can give you their birth date as well of all the Popaj family, over 20 households. But I'm telling you this also, that I didn't know who exactly they were, that they were members of the KLA. But after I returned, in June 1999, when we did the -- when we had the funerals, I saw them in KLA uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Popaj, I think you will have to make up your mind as to the truth of it. Is what you are telling us today the truth and that what you said before was not, given that it is in complete contradiction to what you are saying today?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: I said the same thing earlier. Maybe I did not say when exactly I learned that they were members. I know everybody from the village, the Zhuniqis, the Gashis, and everybody else. But I saw them in uniform when we had the funerals. And I repeat, I know everybody in my village. I knew them then and I know them now.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us the name of these three KLA members that you were talking about?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: Ilir Popaj, Bajram Popaj, and Halim Kelmendi. These were the ones that I saw after the war in uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us what your relationship is with Ilir Popaj and Bajram Popaj? Are you related in any way?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: Yes, they're my relatives. All the Popajs are related.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: You're quite correct about that. Can you explain their kinship to us. Are they close or distant relatives?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: No, they're not close relatives, but we are relatives. We don't live close to each other, but as I said, all the Popajs are related.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Since you explained to us now that you did not see the uniforms before June 1999, can you tell us what the uniforms you did see looked like, the ones you saw at the funeral worn by those KLA members?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: When the funeral was conducted, there were 22 members of the KLA. And to tell you the truth, I was not paying attention to what they were wearing. I had --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction:

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There were 22 members of my family being buried that day, and I did not look at them closely, the ones who were attending.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: How do you know then that they were in uniform?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: Well, I had a look at them and they were in uniform, but after that day I can tell you I never saw them in uniform. I think Bajram still works in defence somewhere. I don't know whether he is wearing a uniform today or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: My question was simply this: Do you remember what the colour of the uniforms was?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: I can't remember the colour, but the investigators from the Tribunal saw them in uniform. And, you know, there are things being said such as Besim Popaj was killed by the KLA and Besim Popaj is still alive. He is a cousin of mine.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Popaj, we only want to learn about what you saw, since this is the matter that we want to get through your testimony. That is why I'm asking you these questions. Let us try to arrive at a conclusion concerning the members of the KLA known by everyone in your village. Did you as a matter of fact ever see them in your village?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: What time are you referring to? I just said that from 1998 to June 1999 I never saw them in the village, because in May 1998 to October 1998 I was in the mountains with the herds. And I went back to the village on the 20th of October. I have 30 cows and I also have a lot of sheep, and I was in the mountains, in the pastures.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Popaj, were there other persons, save for the three whom you mentioned, from your village who were members of the KLA?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: I am not aware of any. If you know of any such members you can ask me, but I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: I would definitely ask you about that. I just wanted to hear from you whether you wanted to share that information with us, perhaps in mentioning everyone I know about I wanted to ask you whether you wanted to tell us something about that first so that I don't omit anyone.

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... I would have for sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: On the 25th of March, 1999, when the police and army entered your village, were there any armed KLA in it?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: No, there weren't.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Popaj, did you know that in the course of 1998 in your village, Bela Crkva, there were KLA members from your village and they were called the civilian protection?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: No, I don't know. I was asked about this other times as well, but I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Did you know that in 1998 the KLA distributed weapons in your village so that the village could defend itself?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: No, I did not know that and that's not true. They did not distribute weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have D004-2607 --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: 2670.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Popaj, this document is a statement by Nesret Popaj given to the OTP to Mr. Gerard Sexton on the 14th of April, 1999. First of all, do you know a person from your village by the name of Nesret Popaj?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: Could you repeat the first name, please, is it Nesret Popaj?

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Exactly, born on the 14th of June, 1963.

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: I know him very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Am I right in saying that Mr. Nesret Popaj was born and lived in Bela Crkva until 1999?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: No, that's not correct. Nesret Popaj in 1994 left Bellacerka and went to Germany, and when he returned I saw him at the funeral on the 5th of July, 1999. During that time, I did not see him in Bellacerka.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: But in 1998, as you told us, you spent most of your time in the mountains with your livestock?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: Well, I'm telling you that he left in 1994. This is not in my statement, but when he left he borrowed some money from me to go to Germany; and then the next time I saw him was in July at the funeral. This is what I know and this is what I'm telling you.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Are you actually explaining to us the reason why he may have chosen not to get in touch with you, given that he had borrowed money from you?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: He borrowed the money in 1994 because he did not have enough money to go to Germany, but three or four months later he returned the money to me. That was just for the trip, for him to go there.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Popaj, if I told you that Nesret Popaj stated that he was a KLA member, would that change anything in your present testimony?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: I don't know whether he was or was not a member of the KLA. If you want information about that, then you ask Nesret Popaj to come here. He still is living in Germany today as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Are you going to change your testimony if I told you that Nesret Popaj stated that the KLA armed your village in 1998 for defence and that he personally was issued with an automatic weapon?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: I don't know about it. My father and Nesret's father are cousins, first cousins, and we would have known. I know that he stayed in Germany from 1994 onwards, and he got his German papers in the year 2000. How could he have been in Kosova? Ahmet, his father, would have told me about him returning. When I came back from the mountains I would have heard about it -- see him.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Popaj, are you going to change your testimony if I tell you that Nesret Popaj stated that he was a member of the civilian protection and armed by the KLA in your village?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: I'm telling you that he wasn't. He couldn't have been. He was not in Kosova in 1998. It's not possible for him to have been there in 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Are you going to change your mind if I tell you that Mr. Nesret Popaj in his statement said that on the 25th of March, 1999, he was in your village and that under his jacket he had a concealed weapon?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: Well, if he said that himself then you invite him to the hearing and he can testify, but I am convinced that he was not in Kosova in 1998/1999. He was there when we started exhuming the bodies and had the funerals. His cousin Xhevdet came to Kosova. I think he went to Germany to pick I am up, and they came to Kosova together for the funeral.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know Avni Popaj from your village? He was Nesret Popaj's cousin, therefore I presume yours as well?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: Yes, they are first cousins, the two of them. I knew them then and I know them now.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Did you know that Avni Popaj -- on the 25th of March, 1999, as Nesret Popaj stated, was in the company of Avni Popaj, his first cousin, as you told us?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: Where were they? Maybe they were, but where were they?

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: So it seems that now they may have been there. Mr. Popaj, up to this point in time you were stating that it was impossible, now you are telling us that there may have been. Am I right in saying that you as a matter of fact do not know whether Nesret Popaj was there or not. At the beginning of your testimony --

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: I'm asking you where were they together? Were they in Albania? Were they in Germany? Where were they together? I'm accepting that they might have been together, but where I'm asking you?

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: You can read my question. Avni Popaj, the 25th of March, 1999, in your village. When Nesret Popaj had that concealed automatic weapon under his jacket, as he himself said, he also shared the information that he was in the company of Avni Popaj. That was my question.

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: None of them were in the village. I think they lied to you or this is your lie.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know Bajram Popaj from your village?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: I knew him then. I know him now, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Is he your cousin?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: All the Popajs are my relatives.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Then I will no longer ask you about the last names, I will go by the first names, although I will point out that these are your relatives. Did you know that Bajram was a KLA member?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: I already told you that I saw him later, but in the Popaj family there are not -- no two names that are the same, and this is the same Bajram Popaj who I saw in June when the bodies were being exhumed, because in the Popaj family there are no two members with the same first name.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Popaj. For clarification, Bajram Popaj was one of the three KLA members from your village that we mentioned at the beginning of this examination; am I correct?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: Yes, I did mention his name, that's correct, but they were not there on the day that you're asking me about.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Now, I didn't put any dates concerning this, Witness. It was about Bajram and Avni --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: Nesret and Avni.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: What about Ilir Popaj, I won't ask you if he's a cousin of yours. He must be since he's from your village. The question is: Is Ilir Popaj from your village and did you know that he was also a KLA member?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: Yes. I already told you that I saw him after the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: So again to clarify, Ilir Popaj that we are discussing now is the second of the three KLA members whom you mentioned when we were discussing, or rather, at the beginning of today's cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: Yes, I did tell you that. Bajram Popaj, Ilir Popaj, and Halim Kelmendi, these are the names that I mentioned earlier and these are the three persons I saw later in 1999 when the bodies were being exhumed.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we next please see D004-2448.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Popaj, this is a diary of Krasniqi Lulezim, commander of the 184th KLA Brigade. I will read out, since it's a voluminous document, I will read out the excerpt from page 8 -- sorry, page 9, paragraph 1: "The plan for the communication maintenance (couriers and radio link) Iljir Popaj and Bajram Popaj and ten more soldiers from Bela Crkva, during the transit towards Jablanica they need to secure the hill ..." This is an order issued by commander of the 184th KLA Brigade. Mr. Popaj, my question for you is this: It is stated here that in addition to Ilir Popaj and Bajram Popaj, for whom you just confirmed to us were KLA members and whom we already discussed, there were another ten KLA members from Bela Crkva. Can you tell us anything about that? Are you familiar with that? Who were those members?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The first question has to be: Do you accept that there were --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: -- ten more members? And you need to indicate to the witness the date, if you have it, of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. The date of the document -- all we have is what is translated and is in e-court. We see at the bottom, page 9, last paragraph, February 1999. I suppose it is between the 30th of January and the 1st of February, 1999, given that this is a diary of the 184th KLA Brigade commander. It was kept daily, hence my conclusion. I don't have a precise date.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You realise you are there giving a great burst of evidence about the document. You may use a document like this to put to the witness, Here is an entry in what appears or purports to be a diary of this KLA unit. If you have it, an approximate date. The passage I have quoted to you suggests that there were, in addition to the two named men, ten other KLA members from the village. Do you accept that? If he doesn't, that's the end of the use you can make of the document until you call evidence to prove there were ten other men. If he accepts there may have been ten other men, you may go on with other questions. It may be that you might like to have a break now to think about how you will use it.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will, Mr. Popaj, have the first break now. That will give you a chance to have a rest. We will continue at 11.00, in half an hour, and the Court Officer will assist you during the break.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Are you all comfortable again there, Mr. Popaj?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Popovic, would you continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I will continue taking on board all of the instructions that I received at the end of the last session.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Popaj, first I'm going to ask you whether you know Lulezim Krasniqi?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: I do not know of him and I have never heard of him.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Do you know anything that Bajram and Ilir Popaj that we mentioned had, or were in the company, or were they in the KLA together with the ten more people from your village, Bela Crkva?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: I am not an investigator. I don't know who these people were. You may ask someone else.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Popaj. I'm going to broach another subject. I'm not going to dwell on this any longer. Mr. Popaj, do you know on the 25th of March, 1999, were they as -- were there any KLA members in Celina or whether it was a stronghold of the KLA at the time?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: On the 25th of May [as interpreted] or after that date, there wasn't any KLA presence or stronghold in the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: I apologise, I'm -- may I repeat that the question concerned the 25th of March and the answer refers to 25th of May.

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: I meant the 25th of March. I said neither on the 25th nor before that date there were any presence.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Please tell us, what is the distance between Celina and your village?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: From my house it is about 1 kilometre and maybe a little bit more. I never measured it actually.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you in your village or in your house hear any fighting if there was any going on in Celina?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: On the 25th of March you couldn't hear anything because of the Serb shelling by the police and the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please tell us what is the distance between Bela Crkva and Nagavci and Rogovo? Let us get some pictures about the distances.

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: Rogove is very close, it is very close from where we are. We are separated only by the stream. I'm talking about Nagavc and Celine. Rogove is not even more than 500 metres away from the place of the massacre.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell us whether Labucevo [Realtime transcript read in error "Lapusnik"] is close to your village?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: I don't know, what do you mean by that? What village do you mean? Are you asking me about Malisheve?

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Not Lapusnik but Labucevo?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: I don't think there is a village by that name. Malisheve, yes, there is a village by this name, and this village is 23 kilometres away from my village.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: It's not necessary to continue. My question referred to the village of Labucevo. If you think such a village does not exist, that is acceptable. My next question is --

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... village by the name of Llapceve. There is no village by this name.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that on the 25th of January, 1999, a KLA member was killed in ambush close to your village, Bela Crkva?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: I don't know. It was in the place between Rahovec, Drenovc, and Potoqan. I have seen that there is a monument erected to that incident.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Did you have any knowledge that in 1998 while you were in the village and at the beginning of 1999, that there were any armed incidents or skirmishes between the KLA and Serb police in, or around, or in the vicinity of your village; and if so, could you tell us what you knew about that?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: It was not in my village. I showed you the road Rahovec-Drenovc-Potoqan, that is where. It is some 16 kilometres from where I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Popaj, most probably you misunderstood me. My question did not refer to that incident. You already covered that in your question -- in your answer. I'm asking you about other events at the end of 1998 and the beginning of 1999. Let me not list them individually. Do you know whether any skirmishes between Serb security forces and the KLA in your village or around your village, so I'm asking you about events which does not -- do not concern that particular incident but some others that you may know of.

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: There were no such skirmishes or fighting in my village.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: And in the immediate vicinity of your village?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: I showed you about that ambush that you mentioned. That was the only one that I know of, where in that place I have seen a monument erected. I don't know of any other incident.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we see, please, D004-2681.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Popaj, could you please take a look at this -- and before that let me ask you: Are you familiar with the book entitled "The Phoenix of Freedom," that would be the translation into Serbian published in Pristina in 2002?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: I have heard about it. It was the Tribunal investigator, whose name I don't remember now, who showed that to me for the first time. He showed that book to me, but I can write a book about you. So I don't think that it's relevant. I told him that what is written in the book is not done with my permission. Probably the author has done it for his own personal profit. I don't know who the author is.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I ask the usher to turn to page 141 of that book. That would be 6D01841. I believe that this is 146. What we need is 141. That is the page. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Popaj, could you please read out the introductory part and then read out the first five names here on the list.

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: I don't need to read it. If I wanted to read it, I would have taken the book that was given to me by this investigator. But I didn't want to have the book. The investigator knows that I didn't take the book because that was done without my permission. I lost a child. I don't need to read anything there. I never spoke with these persons.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Popaj, Mr. Popaj, what I'm asking you is to reply to the questions put to you. I do express my commiseration about you losing a child, but this is not what we're dealing with. Could you read out the introductory part and the first five names you see on the list?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: I don't need to read them because they're not part of my statement, and I've never spoken with such persons. What relevance is that to me?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Popovic, at the moment I would ask the same question as the witness does. I'm sure you must have a reason. I cannot read the language in which the introductory lines are written, so I can't think ahead as to what you may be getting at. I can read the first five names. None of them are names of this witness or of people of his village. They are names that are quite well-known in the organisation of the UCK or the KLA. Now, is there some particular purpose?

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, concerning the witness -- the statement of this witness, the witness has referred to this book earlier. This is not the first time that he's facing this book. This book has been shown to this witness and he answered certain questions asked by the ICTY's investigators. His recent answer was to the effect that he didn't know who wrote the book. This is in Albanian, but I wanted him to read it out so that we can get a translation. This is the editorial board of people who took part in writing this book. He said that he didn't know who the authors were. This is the opportunity to read who the authors were, and then I would be referring to each person mentioned in the book and this will be seen from my further questions, which are connected with the people from his village. He's testified about those things already and everything concerning to that is contained in the Prosecution's evidence disclosed to us. He is quite well aware what people are going to be mentioned hailing from the same villages. He -- as he states, he did not want to take the book from the investigators to see who authored it, but let us see who authored them -- this book. My intention is for him to read out the first five names of the editorial board, and this would be a good introduction to my further questions concerning people from his village who were stated in the book with all their particulars concerning date and place of birth, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Popovic, you can take it that the Chamber is aware that there is a book written by persons not known, but in respect of which book there was an editorial committee of at least 17 leading members of the KLA. They are not authors. They were an editorial committee. Now, I think you can move from there and go straight to any passage that you think ought to be put to the witness, to see whether he accepts the truth of it or has any comment about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Absolutely. I will comply with your suggestions. What I meant to do is to explain to the Court and the witness who the members of the editorial board were. Let's move on. Let's go to page 14. I believe that it's 6D0359.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Popaj, could you please read out what is written here on this page so that we get the translation. This is the chapter that we are going to discuss in my further questioning.

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: I don't see why I should read the title because this was not done with my permission. I don't want to have anything to do with it. That book was brought to me in my own house. I think you've asked me about this topic also the other time I was here. I am now a witness who buried 168 victims with my own hands, men, women, children. You're asking me about the book. Ask those persons who have written the book and not me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Popovic, can I suggest that it might enable you to reach your objective if without asking the witness to read passages you put to him the subject that you want put from the book and see whether he agrees with that or is able to comment on that. From what you have indicated, for example, it may be that you want to say to him: Do you agree that so and so was a member of the KLA? Or: Do you agree that on such and such date there was a KLA action in the village or in the next village or something. I don't know what it is you want to refer to, but you have an emotional problem that is getting in the way of your questioning being effective. And I'm trying to suggest to you ways that you can get past that and get on with the task.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, respecting all what you've said, we have only the Albanian text. We do not have a translation into Serbian. The witness is asked to read it out loud. This is not an emotional problem. It's of a different nature. There's no reason for this witness being granted special status. This is just a title of a chapter, and by reading it out loud he would be explaining or giving us an opportunity for that title to be translated, and then after that we are going to ask some very precise questions without him reading out anything. I wanted to get him to read out in his language so we would get a translation into Serbian and English. And he's already referred to that in the book, in his statement, and in the Milutinovic trial.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Popovic, the Chamber is not minded to oblige the witness to read from this book. Now, either you will find an alternative way of dealing with the problem or move on from there.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. Could we please go to page 23 -- or I'm going to ask you.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: What I just showed you was page 11. Does this refer to heros of the KLA being discussed in that title?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: I am not here to tell you who the martyrs of the KLA were. I'm here to testify to what I saw and experienced myself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Popaj, it would assist this Chamber a great deal if you were able to cooperate with the questions that are being put to you. We respect your concerns, but we must learn some things from you about this book. Now, it's being put to you that there are listed at page 23 a number of people who are said to be heros of the KLA. Perhaps if you could put your glasses on and just have a look to see whether that is what you find on page 23.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They have written these names according to the wish of the author. These are not accurate. If the book was accurate, I would have accepted the book when it was given to me. But there are lies in it. There are untruths in it. When I was asked about Jusuf Popaj during the Milosevic trial whether he was killed by the KLA or not, he was 77 years old, he was a Muslim priest, and he was killed by the Serbs. So this book is the same, is full of untruths. I said, If you leave this book to me - to this investigator - I will burn it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much for that. That has helped us to understand your position quite a bit, Mr. Popaj. There are some other names there which we need to have your comment on. We understand what you have said about Jusuf, and there are probably other explanations you can give about some other names. And then, of course, we will have to assess that in due course. But for the moment could you give any comment you would like to make about other names that are put to you now by Mr. Popovic? Yes, Mr. Popovic, the next name.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: That would be Alban Popaj, born in 1975, do you know him? You can find his name on page 23.

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... 1975. In 1978 he was born on the 16th of April. He is my nephew, the son of my brother. I grew him up -- I raised him because his father died in 1981.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we next see page 67, please.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could Mr. Popovic kindly repeat the ERN reference.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There is a name of a person called Mehmet Popaj born 1954.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Is he from Bela Crkva?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Next, page 86, please.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could Mr. Popovic kindly slowly read the ERN reference number.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: We see the name of Sahit Popaj. Is he from Bela Crkva?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, he was born in 1958.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: This is page --

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: He is my first cousin, my uncle's son.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we see page 94, Shendet Popaj.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Shendet Popaj was my son. He was born on the 8th of November, 1981.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We have only a few pages left. Page 98, Xhavit Popaj.

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: Yes, I know him. I know the people I buried. You don't need to show me the book.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. Popaj. Concerning the book, I have one last question. Page 111, Kreshnik Popaj?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: Yes, Kreshnik Popaj, he was born in 1985 in August.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Popaj. I have no further questions about this book.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you for that assistance, Mr. Popaj. There are things that we need to have your comment on when we come in due course to consider the whole questions that are raised in this trial. So we're grateful for that. Now Mr. Popovic has some other questions.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have a question, please. There is a Qerim Zhuniqi and Fatos Zhuniqi there, my aunt's children, and there were born in -- after 1981, and they have put there their names as KLA members.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction:

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Xhavit and Eqerem [as interpreted] were invalids, they were disabled, how could they have been with the KLA?

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Popaj.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: My next question: Mr. Popaj, did you know that lists were distributed and all those who wanted to be reserve soldiers of the KLA could enter their names on their lists in the course of 1998 and 1999?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: I was not there at that time. Maybe there were lists, but I don't know. Nobody went, though.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Am I right in saying that you spoke to the Tribunal investigators and that it was suggested to you in the course of that interview that on the graves of certain people there were certain inscriptions which were not true? I don't want to prompt you any further, but does this suffice to jog your memory as to that topic discussed with the Tribunal investigators? You spoke about that in the Milutinovic case.

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: Yes, those names were there, but I changed them. I erased them from the list because they don't exist.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you clarify, please. Which names did you change and what was taken off the list since those people did not exist?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: The ones you asked me about. I erased them that year, immediately, because I go every morning to the cemetery. 4.00 in the morning I am there and the Tribunal investigators can keep watch and see me every day when I go there if they want. I was at the cemetery today in the morning at 4.00 before coming here.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Popaj, a clarification, please. Something is unclear to me. Please explain to me what did you erase, what were the names concerned, what were the inscriptions you erased?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: The ones that you mentioned that you said were martyrs and allegedly members of the KLA, they were not. Jusuf Popaj was mentioned there as a martyr. He couldn't have been a member of the KLA. His father was carrying him on his shoulders.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
