utterances.text: Yes, but can you tell us whether on their gravestones it said "martyrs"? Was that the reason -- or is that what you erased from their gravestones?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: Yes. They were martyrs in a sense because they were civilians who died, but they were not fighters.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: So am I right in saying that on their graves it said "martyr," and that after you were suggested that by the Tribunal investigators you erased the word "martyr"?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: They were erased before the book was given to me. These were martyrs, they are all martyrs, but civilians because -- in fact, if you say "hero" or a fighter, a fallen hero, then those are members -- those could be members of the KLA. How could my son who was 14 years old be a member of the KLA or Kreshnik? He was not even 14 years old at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Popaj. That was my question I was trying to clarify, that is to say that on the gravestones it said "fallen fighters" or "fallen heros," and that it was suggested that such inscriptions should be taken off. Am I correct in saying that? This is a specific question that I have.

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: It says there "martyrs." All of them have that inscription.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Popaj. Now to go back to the 1999 statement. In the continuation of paragraph 4 you say in the last sentence that: "Previously, like most inhabitants of the village, I provided food and money for the KLA ..." When did you give money or food for the KLA for the first time?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: In 1998 the whole village gave money and whatever they had. Somebody gave more, some people gave less. It was the old man of the village that came from house to house and asked for those assistance -- for those aids.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. On how many occasions did you provide food or money for the KLA?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: I never gave them money. I only gave meat. Even if they come today that's what I would give them because I have a cow-shed full of cows. People gave money according to their -- to their ability, how rich they were. Mustafe Gashi was the representative of the village and he collected the money. I don't know how much money he collected. He knows.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Given that the village elder collected the money and food, am I right in saying that this was done in an organised fashion to collect money and food for the KLA at the level of the village?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: I don't know whether it was organised or not. They came to my house and asked for contributions. I asked them, What do you need? And I -- and they said, Whatever you have. And I had 600 kilogrammes of meat and I gave it to them.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: When you say "they came to my house," can we clarify who it was. Who was it that came to your house and asked for you to contribute, as you put it?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: I said Mustafe Gashi, the representative of the village, he was the one who came.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Did Mustafe Gashi as the village representative go to the other inhabitants of the village with the same request or did he only come to you?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: I don't know. I didn't ask him. It was none of my business whether he went elsewhere or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Do you recall that in the Milutinovic case you said that other inhabitants of the village also contributed in accordance with their ability?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: Yes. All the inhabitants of the village contributed. It was not only me that contributed. They all gave whatever they had. It was not an obligation to give this amount of money or that amount of money. Whatever they had they could give if they had it.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Based on this answer, Mr. Popaj, am I right in saying - and this will round off the topic of the KLA - that you were a KLA sympathiser and that you supported them in 1998 and 1999?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: Who would not love their own army? Not only our own army, but even when the KFOR came after the war they entered Kosova, we helped them, I helped them.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Popaj, am I right in saying that you assisted them in both 1998 and 1999 and that as a matter of fact you were given certain tasks? There was also a fact from your statement whereby you say that you had a pair of binoculars in your bag. Was that one of your tasks concerning your collaboration with the KLA?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: I had those particulars from 1973 when I started going to Sharri pastures. I have three shepherds there who stay with the sheep in the mountains now and they all have binoculars themselves.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Popaj. My next question before we go back to your 1999 statement is this: Do you recall being heard by an investigative judge of the Prizren court in the proceedings against the accused Andjelko Kolasinac from Orahovac?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: Yes, I went there together with my wife, to Prizren. My wife was pregnant at the time, and I went with her.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Do you recall whether you provided a statement to the court or your wife?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: My wife was supposed to give testimony, but she left the room because she couldn't. She was heavily pregnant at the time. And then I testified in her place. But my testimony was not accepted.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In that testimony or statement, did you enumerate certain people whom you personally see open fire at Nasije [phoen] when discussing the event in your village of the 25th of March, 1999, which took place under the bridge? You also described that in your statement?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: I saw them opening fire on the Zhuniqi family, the 14 members of that family. Then they opened fire on Halim Fetoshi. He was born in 1932. And then the big group at the Belles bridge were executed. We went to the place of the execution, and we took pictures. Where are those pictures? And we also hung up their boots and their shoes on a tree there. They took pictures. Where are those pictures? They brought Andjelkovic by helicopter there to see where they committed the crime.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Popaj; however, that was not my question. My question was this: Did you enumerate certain people by their first and last names as the people you saw carry out the massacre at the Belles bridge?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: I mentioned the names according to what Feim Popaj told me. In the beginning, they killed two people. Feim Popaj is alive but he's not well in his head now. He survived the massacre but he's not well.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Am I right in saying that in the Milutinovic case you stated that you did not see or recognise any of the persons who committed the massacre?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: I did not recognise any of them because I was not close to them -- I was not close enough. I was about 120 metres away on the other side of the stream. When they executed the 14 people, one of them survived, 13 died.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Am I right in saying that in your testimony you mentioned Cedomir Jovanovic, stating that you saw him open fire at Nasije when you were discussing that event? Cedomir Jovanovic.

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: As a dead person? I told you that Feim told me everything because I couldn't myself see. There are still traces there where the execution happened. Even if you go there today you will see traces of the execution. You can go and see for yourself where the people were executed and where I was and where the people who executed them were. It was not possible for me to see. The traces are still there, though. You can go for yourself.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Popaj. Am I right in saying that in that statement you say that you personally saw Cedomir Jovanovic open fire at Nasije when you discussed the crime of the 25th of March, 1999. That is my question. Am I right in saying that?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: Those were the ones who opened fire, the ones who were on my side of the stream. They opened fire against the group of 14 people, and then the group of 46 men few metres further, they were all executed there. They executed children and women. They executed 2-year-olds.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Please focus on my question. You said a minute ago that you couldn't recognise anyone, given that you were not close enough. You were 120 metres away, lines 9 and 10 of the previous page of the transcript. Now I'm asking you this: In your testimony before the investigative judge in Prizren, did you say that you saw Cedomir Jovanovic --

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: I told you I was 120 metres away. The distance was measured. You can go there yourself and measure it. And the stream was in between.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Popaj. I'll move on to my next topic. In your June 1999 statement in paragraph 6 you say that: One week before the NATO bombardment, Serb police and soldiers came to your village ... My question is this: Except for the policemen and soldiers at that time as well as on the 25th of March, 1999, did you see any other or additional members of the police?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: Any additional members of Serb forces except for the policemen and soldiers.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There were patrols on other days; however, they came on the 22nd of March and opened trenches with excavators at Naim Fetoshi's house, and they told Naim Fetoshi and his members of the family, there were 38 of them, to leave their house. And they stationed there -- and above the house of Naim Fetoshi on the hill they opened the trenches. I'm telling you about all the things that I know. It was on the 22nd that they came, 22nd of March. And the trenches are still there. I can take pictures if you want.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. That is already in your statement. Could you please answer my questions because this would save us time and we would conclude more quickly. We have all that in your statement. My question is this and I'll try to be specific: On the 25th of March did you have an opportunity to see -- Mr. Popaj, please wait until I finish my question and then answer.

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: I will answer all the questions that you have about my statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: If we both speak at the same time, we'll do nothing. Am I right in saying that on the 25th of March, 1999, you saw members of the paramilitary in your village?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: I saw Serb policemen and army members. I don't know what you mean by the word "paramilitaries." I'm talking of the Serb army and police.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's take a look at Exhibit P01083, please, page 5753, lines 5 and 6. That would be the Milutinovic case transcript. Transcript page 5753, lines 5 and 6.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Asked whether you saw paramilitaries you answered: "Yes, I did ... it was the paramilitaries who did the execution of the 74 people from" my "village; it wasn't me who did" that. My question is: Did you see paramilitaries on the 25th of March, 1999, in your village?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: From the 25th to the 4th of May, every single day, because they started from the 25th and they ended setting fire to the houses on the 4th of May. They were there until the 4th of May. On the 4th of May they went to the hill in the direction of the road that leads to Potoqan.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: If I could just --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Every single day I saw them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Behar.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Your Honours. Just before we continue on that point, if my friend is going to be putting a question about the paramilitaries from the Milutinovic transcript I think it's also fair to take the witness to the passage in which he's asked specifically what he means by paramilitary, that's at page 5766 of the transcript, beginning at line 19.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] By "paramilitaries," I mean those people who kill others.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, may we continue? The witness just expressed his opinion on what he understood paramilitaries to mean.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The critical issue appears to be the one that is dealt with in the questions of Judge Bonomy at page 5766, and in particular the answer on page 5767, where this witness said the people he's calling paramilitaries were part of the official police. They were brought there in vehicles. They didn't come on foot.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, you're absolutely right, but the Defence holds that this is a matter to be dealt with by my learned friend in his re-direct. My question to the witness was whether Mr. Popaj saw paramilitaries or not, and I absolutely agree that he may express his opinion about what he means the word "paramilitaries" mean -- means. I'm going to move on to another topic.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Popaj, could you explain to us how members of the police and the army looked like, what uniforms they wore on the 25th of March, 1999; and if you could tell them apart, what was it that enabled you to tell them apart?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: I could distinguish them because the police were wearing lighter camouflage colours. The army was wearing camouflage colours but of a darker hue. I already explained that. But I was to blame for not taking them at Fetoshi's house, the uniforms, like the maps.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Popaj.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we see D002-5109 to be shown, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Popaj, now we are going to show you different patterns of military uniforms. Please take a look at them and tell us whether any of the patterns correspond to the patterns that you saw on the 25th of March, 1999, as worn by -- as a part of the uniform worn by either police or the military.

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: I didn't see them only on that day. I told you, I saw them until the 4th of May. Every single day in the village I saw them. In the village until the 4th of May I saw these people.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. All the easier it will be for you to recognise some of these patterns. Could you please tell us whether any of the patterns shown here corresponds to what you saw. The number is D002-5109, but let me double-check.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And that number is on the Defence exhibit list, on the list that the Defence has indicated it will be using.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This -- the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Only that page?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: Wait a little until I put on my glasses because I can't see them well. This is the picture of the Serb uniforms, the army uniforms.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Could you put a circle around that one, please, Mr. Popaj.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can do it right away.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Do that now, please, and put a number 1 against that if you would. Now, are there any others there that you recognise of those camouflage patterns?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will circle all those uniforms that I have seen then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Now, number 1 you said was a pattern that you said was a Serb army uniform. The other patterns that you have circled, can you tell us what uniforms they were?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] These were the uniforms of the Serb police both I have encircled here, both the army and the police, four circles.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Four circles. Could you use number 1 for the Serb army and number 2 for the Serb police. From what you are saying --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Also for the army. This is the uniform they were wearing. Number 2, so number 1 and number 2 I think belonged to the army uniforms.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. 1 and 2 you've circled are army. Now, you've also circled two others. Are they the uniforms you believe of the Serb police?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will explain. Those who came with Pinzgauers at the house of Fetoshi, 1 and 3, they came with these clothes. Those who forced the family members to leave the house. The others were the uniforms of the people with tanks stationed in the school-yard until the 4th of May. They were wearing the uniform that is indicated in number 2.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We can't see at the moment whether you have circled any more than three uniforms. Have you circled more than three?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have made four circles.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Right. You've told us what numbers 1, 2, and 3 are. Could you tell us now what number 4 is, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Number 4 shows the uniform that I saw on the 12th or 13th of April. They were with the armoured car and the truck, those that brought these eight corpses from Rahovec to be buried in Celine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. The Court Officer will, of course, bring that original exhibit back with him and it will be marked as an exhibit. Now, are there more issues you want to question about that, Mr. Popovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just one, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell us which of the four that you encircled was the uniform of the police?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: This one, the third.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Popaj.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The Court Officer will give an exhibit number now so that there is less room for confusion.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the marked photograph will be given exhibit number D00314.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, am I right in saying that in your today's statement you said that after the event under the bridge you did not go to Zrze with your mother, father, and sister?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: I am not Mr. Zhuniqi. I am Mr. Popaj. You have mixed it up.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: I apologise. Right -- I apologise for misspeaking your name, but the question is the same. Is it true that in today's testimony you said that you did not with your wife, mother, and father go to Zrze after the incident at the bridge or under the bridge?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: After the event, I did not go until the tractor came. When the tractor came, I went to Xerxe together with the wounded persons. I said I didn't go when we went to Albania, when my wife went to Albania. I think you are mixing it up.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Popaj, I'm going to read out what you said in 1999. Page 5, paragraph 2, in the Serbian version. "We, my mother, father, wife, then walked to Xerxe after that." So in 1999 you state that you went to Zrze.

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: We went along with the tractor. The tractor drove. We followed the tractor walking. When we loaded the wounded, my wife, my father, my mother, and my aunt, along with myself, we all followed the tractor on foot.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: This is what you stated today. I'm going to read out what you stated in 1999. It was something different. In 1999 in the same paragraph you said: "Two villagers volunteered to return to the scene with a tractor and trailer and bring the survivors back to Xerxe, Abaz Kryeziu and Shemsedin Kelmendi accompanied by father Selim, wife Fidaije, and aunt Zymryde back to the scene of the execution to bring back the survivors. They went on the tractor owned by Abaz Kryeziu. After about one hour they returned with the survivors on the trailer." So you never mentioned yourself as somebody who left Zrze?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: -- all returned.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, but in the first sentence, Mr. Popaj, you say: "We, my mother, father, wife, and I then walked to Xerxe. On arrival I saw that the other women, children, and old men had arrived safely in the village." So you claim that you arrived to Zrze. You say "on arrival." This is what you stated in 1999. Today you are stating something else. Am I right in saying so?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: I said even then that when we went to Xerxe we were together with the wounded persons, all of us. It was there, in Xerxe, that I met my brother, his children, his wife, my brother's wife and children. I saw all the women who were there and everything that I mentioned in my statement. There was also Fedaije [phoen], Fatos' wife, the mother of Labinot Zukiqi [phoen]. I haven't mentioned that in my statement, but I'm telling you now. I would like to invite the usher to give you your June 1999 statement, that is P01082 on page 6 in the Albanian.

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: I read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Below the names there begins a paragraph where you state that you went to Zrze, that you arrived there, and that after that, after your arrival, your father, Abaz Kryeziu, and Shemsedin Kelmendi, together with your wife and aunt, went back to the execution site to bring back the survivors. You can read it for yourself since you today are stating something completely different. Am I right in saying so?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: I have already stated, even during the Milutinovic case, that they came with a tractor. We went to the scene of the event and we loaded the wounded persons on to the tractor, and then we returned to Xerxe.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Popaj, I'm asking you about your 1999 statement and you stated yourself that your memory was the freshest then, having been taken at three months after the event. What you stated in that statement is -- does not correspond to what you are saying today. Is it -- what I'm asking you to say is: What is the truth, what you said back in 1999 or what you're saying today, because those two stories are not identical?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: I didn't have a good -- fresh memory then because at that time I weighed 37 kilogrammes. I was not in a good health condition at that time. I was -- I weighed simply 37 kilogrammes. I'm telling you what happened, how people came there, how we went to fetch the victims, the wounded persons, and so on. You can ask even the other persons who were present; they can tell you the same story.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Popaj, the questions to follow concern Mr. Zhuniqi and this is why I mixed up your names. Please, since you do not -- did not have a very good memory back in 1999 - and this is the basis for my examination - please tell us the following things. You gave a statement in 1999 and then in 2002, after that in 2006 and we went through that at the beginning of my cross-examination. I have not found Mr. Isuf Zhuniqi being mentioned in either of those statements or testimonies; am I right?

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Sorry for the interruption, Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't mention Isuf Zhuniqi --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Behar --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- because he came here himself and gave testimony and he also stated that he met me then.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: I apologise for the interruption, Your Honour. Mr. Zhuniqi was actually mentioned in the Milutinovic transcript, and with just a moment's indulgence I can find that reference.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, if you think that this would be a good time for a break, we can in the meantime help my learned friend to find the reference and then continue after that. I'm going to make sure that my cross-examination is finished as soon as possible after we resume after the break, 20 minutes to 30 minutes tops.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Popaj, we'll have another break now to give you another chance for a rest, and we continue at 1.00. So we'll have another break now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Popaj, we continue now. Mr. Popovic has a few more questions. Mr. Popovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, before I begin I wanted to draw your attention to something. Mr. Behar pointed out a page in -- at which Mr. Popaj mentions Mr. Zhuniqi. It is page 5669 in the Milutinovic case, line 8 and line 9. While on that topic, could the Court Officer please put P01083 on the screen which is a page of the transcript from the Milutinovic case, page 5669.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Popaj, I have a question about Isuf Zhuniqi, you mentioned him at page 5669, lines 8 and 9. You said: "We heard Isuf Zhuniqi screaming" or yelling. You did not mention where he was at that point. As one of the survivors, you did not mention him as one of the persons on the list of the survivors you compiled; am I correct?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: We don't have any audio.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Is it the case that you cannot hear us?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can hear you now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, Mr. Popovic will ask again his question.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Popaj, in your previous statements you did not say where Mr. Isuf Zhuniqi was and you did not mention him as one of the survivors. Am I correct in saying that?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: I did not mention him because he was not on the tractor. The statement contains the names of the people who were loaded on the tractor as survivors. He left the place of the execution before we took the wounded. Isuf Zhuniqi was there, and I mentioned that in my statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: I will use this opportunity to read again from page 4 of your statement of 1999, the last paragraph. You mention your wife and you say, She returned some 20 minutes later telling me that nine people survived the execution. She named the following persons, and there you mentioned the names. There you did not mention that any of them were on the tractor. You referred to them as those who survived the execution. Can you clarify this discrepancy between what was said then and now? I.e., you mentioned fine survivors without mentioning --

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... discrepancy, sir. I have explained very clearly when we went there -- in fact, it was my wife that saw them first, but we went and loaded them on the tractor. After that, we went to Xerxe to Abaz Kryeziu's house, and -- except for Sezai Zhuniqi who died in 2006, Alban Popaj and --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not catch the name of the second person --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- who died on the same day. One on the 25th and one on the 26th of May -- of March.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Popaj, this is what you said today and it does not tally with what you said in 1999. You say that your wife told you of nine survivors. You mentioned the first and last names of those people. Never did you mention that these nine people returned to Xerxe with you on that tractor. You just say that she told you there were nine survivors. We have their first and last names. Among those, we don't find Isuf Zhuniqi. So you never said those people were on that tractor in the statement of 1999. Can you clarify that?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: I always mentioned that these people were transported by tractor to Xerxe. When we saw Isuf Zhuniqi we were at the train tracks, and Isuf Zhuniqi was walking and screaming and he -- we understood from his gestures that they had been executed. Then they went to Xerxe and Abaz Kryeziu and Kelmendi came back, and we took those persons who survived the massacres. When we went to Xerxe, Hysni Popaj died and Alban Popaj died the next day in the early hours of the morning. Then another person died in 2006 which was Sezai Zhuniqi.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Popaj, you have already repeated that on several occasions today. I am trying to focus on your statement of 1999. If need be, the Court Officer can provide you with the statement for you to remind yourself. If you explain to me that at that time you were unable to recollect everything clearly, I will accept that as your answer, but can you please focus on my questions since you seem to be repeating yourself. You seem to be answering a question that was not put. In any case, let's not dwell on that any longer. In your statement at page 7, paragraph 6, you say that five minutes after the event under the bridge you heard of a third shooting which took place but that you did not see any of it. Am I right in saying that concerning the third incident in which you supposed six people were killed whom you found later, a day later, am I right in saying that everything you told us about that incident is merely an assumption on your part?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: I did not see the killing, but I saw the persons when I buried them. They were Hysni Zhuniqi, Sedat Popaj, Irfan Popaj, Nirsi [as interpreted] Zhuniqi, and Agim Zhuniqi, that I buried with my own hands, 85 metres away from the first place.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Popaj, am I right in saying that you were not an eye-witness and that you have no direct knowledge about the way that these people were killed and whom you buried later on when we are talking about groups of people?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: Six persons. This was the Muslim priest of the village, the Dervish, the -- my cousins were in that group. And I can give you their dates of birth if you want.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Obviously you did not understand the question. My question was this: Am I right in saying that you were not an eye-witness and that you have no direct knowledge about the way these people were killed, the people you found and buried? I'm not referring to the event that you have described already --

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... not an eye-witness, but I heard the shots. I thought in the beginning that they were just shooting in the air, but Muharrem Zhuniqi told me on the 27th in the evening, and then I went there and found them. It was not my father who killed them. It was the same policeman who killed the previous group that killed them again.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Those were your assumptions and you have already testified to that. What was missing from my question was this, and it was not interpreted: Am I right in saying that you were not an eye-witness and that you have no direct knowledge about the way the people you found and buried in Celine, to the effect, how they were killed? I tried to put that question several times. I mean Celine itself.

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... heard the shot, and I buried them myself. I did not eye-witness the killing. I heard the shots, and I buried them myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: In your statement, Mr. Popaj, you say that in Celine you found and buried 84 corpses; am I correct?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know a person by the name Jemini Agim?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: Yes, I know him. It was with him that I buried those people.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Is your testimony going to change if I tell you that Jemini Agim was heard before this Tribunal. In that testimony, he said he found and buried 78 victims during the 21 days of burials?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: Agim was not there when we buried the other seven people. He did not mention them. I can give you the names if you want. We found five in a basement and then also some other people, two other people, in a garage.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: In -- from the previous sentence, page 66, line 2, you said you know him and that he was the person who was with you when you were burying those people. That is why I was asking you that question. Given that we are short of time, I am about to move to another topic. At page 9 of your statement, the last paragraph in B/C/S --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could Mr. Popovic kindly repeat the references in the English and Albanian versions.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Certainly. The references are as follows: Page 10, paragraph 4 in the English; page 13, paragraph 4 in the Albanian.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: You say the following: I heard the sound of jet aircraft in low flight. After several seconds you heard four strong detonations. You went to the village of Nagavc and you discovered a house completely destroyed and four seriously damaged. Mr. Popaj, the houses -- or first of all, did you see the craters created by the bombs dropped there and do you bring the four explosions and destroyed houses in connection with the low-flying aircraft?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: Yes, I heard them. It was -- it was about twenty to 2.00 after midnight, and we went there to Nagavc to see what had happened. No tiles had remained on the roofs, and we couldn't hear anything. That day, we went back to where we were staying. We went to Feim Elshani's yard later on, and there we found Sanije Kasapi [phoen] dead. And two days later we found eight children under 10 years old in one of the houses who had been killed by the explosion. I have explained this in my statement as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Am I right in saying that the explosion that you referred to killing the persons you mentioned was actually caused by the bombs dropped from the low-flying aircraft; is that your statement?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Did you know that there is a report of the MUP staff of the Republic of Serbia about the event of the 2nd of April, 1999, when NATO forces bombed the village of Nagavc, and that on that occasion 11 persons were killed?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: I don't know, but I don't think it was NATO planes. NATO planes dropped bombs between Rogove and Xerxe, and it was during the day.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: And hence you conclude that NATO aircraft did not drop those bombs, given that it was night-time and it was not between Rogovo and Xerxe?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: You may ask the NATO commander at -- who was then the commander. Maybe he has taken shells from Milosevic and has dropped them there, but these were Serbian-make shells. You are saying that it was NATO who dropped them and not Serbia, maybe they bought it from the Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... basis -- can you tell us what is the basis for you to claim that these were Serbian-made bombs?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: Because they had Cyrillic letters written on the -- these shells.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you read the Cyrillic script, Mr. Popaj?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: I have started to learn it now. I can't read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: I am not asking you about now --

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... no --

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: -- I am interested in 1999. At that time, could you read Cyrillic?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: Yes, I went to school. For eight years I was taught Serbian. Of course I knew how to read Cyrillic.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: At line 6 of the same page, that is to say half a minute ago, you said that you started to learn the Cyrillic script and that you still cannot read it. What has changed in the half a minute? When did you learn to read Cyrillic?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: I already told you. You're asking me irrelevant questions. I told you that the shells were Serbian make. After my return from The Hague I went to Elshani and asked him to bring these shrapnels, the remainders, and bring them here to this Tribunal. You might ask Feim Elshani, because I went to his house after I returned from here in 2006. Right from the airport I went to his house to see these shrapnels myself and you might have read it yourself had you seen these shrapnels.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge of Mr. Elshani being asked about that upon your return in 2006, whereupon he said he was not in possession of any bomb parts with any Cyrillic inscriptions?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: He has told you that they were taken by the German KFORs and that the shells, when they were taken from him, that present was also someone, Arbour, I don't know what the name is, from the Tribunal, when we exhumed 16 members of the Myftari family.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Popaj, did you know that NATO conducted an internal investigation. There is not a single part such as the one you describe that were handed over to the German KFOR. Do you have any information regarding that? This document is something we received from the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: I have no information about that because ten years have passed since then, and my belief was that these parts were there. Feim didn't want to give these parts to me. He wanted -- he told me that he wanted to keep them for himself, but then the German KFOR came and they took it away. I'm not an expert on army matters.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: I'm -- I know that, Mr. Popaj. That's why I'm not asking you about military issues. My last question on this topic then is: Do you know what it was that the Cyrillic sign said? Which were the letters you could see?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: I don't remember, but I know that they were Serbian shells. Only Serbia uses Cyrillic letters.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Popaj. Can you tell us the exact date when the mosques in Bela Crkva, Celine, Rogovo were blown up, as you say?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: On the 28th of March. It was a day of Bajram.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Are you going to change your statement if I tell you that Jemini Agim spoke on the same circumstances before the Tribunal and he said that in Celine the mosque was destroyed on the 30th or the 31st of March, 1999?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: It was on the 28th when the three mosques were shelled. Bashkim Jemini was in hiding. He didn't see anything, together with Jusuf Jemini. I was there in a field from where you can see all over. You can see the mosque. Even today you can see the mosque. We have built a new one.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Just to clarify matters. My question referred to Agim Jemini, and you referred to Bashkim and Jusuf Jemini. But my question concerned Agim Jemini. Did you mean him when you said that he was hiding in the basement and didn't see anything?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: Yes, I meant Agim and Jusuf Jemini. They are my first cousins.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: They were at the attic when their family were killed in the basement.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Popaj. My next question: Is it known to you that the mosques in your village and the surrounding villages were used as KLA strongholds?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: I don't know that -- have built them from the beginning now. Do you think we have built the new mosques to be used as military bases? Now we have extended the area of the mosques from 46 to 56 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: All questions I put to you concern 1999, or rather, the end of 1998 and 1999. So what you are discussing is not the matter I'm asking you about. I would like to ask the Chamber for their indulgence. I'm sure that I can finish in five to ten minutes, and then give some time for Mr. Behar for his re-direct. I'm going to make sure that this is quick, as quick as possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You will have to be quicker than that because we finish at a quarter to and Mr. Behar must re-examine by then. So you identify what is important and deal with it very quickly.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Absolutely. I've discussed this with Mr. Behar before we resumed about what he needed for his re-direct, and I'm going to act accordingly. D004-2765, can we see it on the e-court, please. 004-2675, so it's the last four digit 2675.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: And before we see it on the screen let me tell you, it is a book published by the state archives of Kosovo, the sector of the KLA archives, prepared by Nusret Plana and published by Grafo Print Shop at Pristina. Mr. Emin Kabashi is a redactor, also a witness in these proceedings, and there is an editorial committee on page 3, Adem Demaqi, Agim Qeku, Mr. Kabashi -- I'm not going to list all of them. My question, if the Chamber permits me, would concern page 4 in e-court, that would be page 412 of the book in question, and I would like to ask Mr. Popaj to tell us whether he can recognise the mosque, or rather, the picture and tell us whether this depicts the mosque at Rogovo.

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: It is not the Rogove mosque, this one.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Could I please ask you to read out - and I don't -- I hope it's not going to be a problem - what is written below under item 4, or rather, I could tell you. It is a mosque built in 1578, built in Rogove e Hasit. Is this the Rovogo that we are dealing with right now?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: We have another photo of this mosque. Maybe this is an aerial picture. We have repaired the destroyed mosque. We have retained the foundations and have built on them. You can take a picture of a mosque from anywhere, but to me this is not the Rogove mosque.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: So you claim that this is not the Rogovo mosque. Let us be as precise as possible because the following questions stem from the issue of the Rovogo mosque.

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: No, it is not. It writes Rogove -- the Rogove mosque, but this is not the picture that I know of the Rogove mosque. Every village had a mosque that was destroyed.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, may I move to adduce this into evidence?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D00315, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I would suggest you have one more question, Mr. Popovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Absolutely, Your Honours. This is my last question.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Popaj, could you please describe for us what members of the police looked like at the border crossing when you were crossing over to Albania? Could you please describe their uniforms? And you mentioned an inscription "policija" or "police." Could you please specify where it was written, in which script, how, and some more details about that?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: I was not an expert to look closely at them. I saw the "policija" written on the arm and in the jacket -- on the jacket, here and here. I was not there for pleasure, and I was not an expert.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Popaj. This would conclude my cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. I apologise to my learned friend for shortening his re-direct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Behar.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Your Honours. I did speak to my friend previously and indicated that I had less than ten minutes of questions which is accurate. I think hopefully I can do this in five to ten minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Sir, you were asked some questions earlier about Isuf Zhuniqi and about that list of survivors that's at page 5 of your statement that was given in June of 1999. My question for you is that when you saw Isuf Zhuniqi, can you tell us, did you see him before your wife went back to the stream and then identified those nine survivors that she saw there?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: Yes, I saw him before.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: So then to put that another way, when your wife went to the stream and saw those nine people, Isuf Zhuniqi had run away already?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: Yes, he had already run away. He was no longer there. That is the truth.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Is that why he was not included in that list?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: Yes. I didn't include his name because when I was asked, the question was: Who did you take on top of the tractor? How many persons did you lead onto this tractor? And that's why I didn't mention him. I mentioned the persons that we loaded onto the tractor, those that we carried to the other village.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Also a few moments ago you were asked a couple of questions about Agim Jemini. I was just looking back at the transcript -- one of the transcript references, and I noted that Mr. Jemini said that he believed it was six or seven days after the 24th of March that the mosque was bombed. I wanted to put that to you accurately. But my question for you, sir, is that: You mentioned that Agim Jemini, you believed, was in the attic when his family was killed in the basement; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: This is what Agim Jemini told me, and I am repeating his words. We went to look for his family to bury -- members, to bury them, and we didn't find them. We found two other bodies, Isad Dini [as interpreted] and his brother. We found them in the yard of Jahir Rexhepi.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. And that's what I was going to ask you. I was going to ask how you knew that information about Mr. Jemini. So am I correct in understanding that he had told you that he was in the attic when his family was killed in the basement; is that right?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: That's correct. This is what he told me, that he heard the shots. He was together with Isufi in this attic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And if I'm understanding you correct then, sir, did he tell you that during this period in 1999 and then were you saying that you then after he told you that went with him to look for the bodies; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Did you find those bodies?

utterances.speaker: SABRI POPAJ
utterances.text: No, we found them at a later time in Rahovec, after our return. They were executed and their bodies taken to Rahovec.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Those are my questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thanks to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Popaj, you'll be pleased to know that that concludes the questions of the Chamber. We have your statement and your previous evidence as well as what you have said today, and we will give those full consideration in due course. We're thankful for your assistance and what you've been able to say today to clarify a number of issues. The Court Officer will assist you now, but that concludes your evidence today. Tomorrow we will be dealing with another witness from Pristina. So we thank you again for your assistance.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I want to thank you, Your Honours. I apologise if sometimes I have made some mistakes, but I want to thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will now adjourn for today and continuing at 9.00 in the morning. May I mention that as we sit at 9 tomorrow we must finish the videolink of the remaining witness tomorrow. The parties need to be aware of that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 15th day of July, 2009, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.46 p.m.,
